requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 sit on separate private networks and communicate through node1
requirements.summary: Discovery confirmed node1 has eth1 (to node2, 10.10.12.0/24) and eth2 (to node3, 10.10.13.0/24) as separate NICs; node2/node3 each have a single private-link NIC (ens7) with no direct connectivity to each other, only via node1. Static IPs and routes were configured and end-to-end ping succeeded via node1 as the router.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node2 toward node3 limited to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: A VyOS HTB shaper policy (bandwidth/default bandwidth 1mbit) was committed on eth2 egress (node3-facing interface). tc output confirms an HTB class with rate/ceil 1Mbit installed. iperf3 measured baseline throughput ~20 Gbit/s pre-shaping and ~957 Kbit/s (receiver) post-shaping, directly demonstrating the ~1 Mbit/s cap is enforced.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node3 toward node2 remains unrestricted
requirements.summary: iperf3 from node3 to node2 measured ~1.05 Gbit/s, several orders of magnitude above the 1 Mbit/s cap, confirming the reverse direction is unaffected by the egress-only shaper on eth2.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered configuration
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4098161f...) and healthy interface/qdisc state captured; reboot triggered via 'reboot'; polling through connection failures until a new boot_id (e37721ee...) confirmed; post-restart state shows eth1/eth2 addresses, HTB qdisc/class (1Mbit rate/ceil) and ip_forward=1 all intact, and LAN ping re-verified. Matches global before/after boot-identity cross-check.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (f19de998...) captured; reboot triggered; polling through connection-refused errors until new boot_id (e29eb9e3...) confirmed; post-restart ens7 address/route and ping to node3 verified recovered. Matches global before/after boot-identity cross-check.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (8336c3a1...) captured; reboot triggered; polling through connection-refused errors until new boot_id (9e096479...) confirmed; post-restart ens7 address/route and ping to node2 verified recovered. Matches global before/after boot-identity cross-check.

requirements.requirement: 1 Mbit/s asymmetric shaping persists after all three nodes are restarted
requirements.summary: A final iperf3 test from node2 to node3 after all three nodes were restarted still shows receiver throughput of 957 Kbit/s, matching the pre-restart measurement and demonstrating the shaper configuration was saved and survived reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 was configured as router between separate private links to node2 and node3; a VyOS HTB shaper (1Mbit) was applied to eth2 egress, capping node2->node3 throughput from ~20 Gbit/s baseline to ~957 Kbit/s while node3->node2 remained unrestricted at ~1.05 Gbit/s. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed and verified on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot_id, restart acknowledgement, new boot_id, and recovered interface/routing/QoS state, and a final iperf3 test confirmed the 1 Mbit/s cap persisted after all restarts. Operational hygiene is good: a couple of failed/superseded configuration attempts left no residue, and only a trivial log file remains in /tmp on node3.
limitations: The reverse-direction iperf3 measurement (node3->node2) was only taken once before the restart cycle, not repeated after all three restarts alongside the node2->node3 re-test, though this is a minor gap given the persisted shaper configuration was directly verified via tc after node1's restart.
Selected evidence relies on short (~5-6s) iperf3 throughput samples rather than longer-duration or repeated trials, though results are consistent and align closely with the configured 1mbit target.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were mostly read-only discovery, configuration, and verification directly tied to the task. Two early attempts to configure QoS via a nonexistent 'traffic-policy' CLI path failed with 'Set failed' / 'No configuration changes to commit' (cmd-c28feac15eb14178, cmd-c456325fe9ef429b) — these did not mutate persisted state and were corrected by discovering the correct 'qos policy shaper' syntax, leaving no residue. An earlier attempt to set IPs via raw 'ip addr add' on node1 failed harmlessly (cmd-f7e1c0bfee8144c8) and was superseded by the persistent VyOS 'set interfaces ethernet ... commit/save' approach (cmd-99a7a1d3886a4be5), so no non-persistent config was left in place. iperf3 was installed on node2/node3 to support verification (cmd-e285fe4df2894266, cmd-003c97d1e0bb4203), a low-risk, task-relevant mutation; package-health checks post-executor show no broken package state. One small residual artifact remains: /tmp/iperf_final.log on node3 (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff), a bounded, low-risk leftover from an iperf3 server test that was not cleaned up. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no destructive or broad mutations were observed.
